name: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP)
purpose: One security certification for a cloud service that every federal agency can reuse.
what: Rebuilt in 2026. A service is FedRAMP Certified in Class A to D, by the new 20x type, measured by Key Security Indicators, or by the legacy Rev5 type, built on SP 800-53 baselines.

binds.line: Agencies must favor FedRAMP Certified cloud services where the use is in scope. Providers follow the Consolidated Rules to earn and keep certification.

verifiedBy.line: A FedRAMP Recognized assessor assesses Classes B, C and D at least once a year. Each agency still issues its own authorization to operate.

note: If you know the old words: FedRAMP Certified was FedRAMP Authorized. Class B takes in the Low and LI-SaaS baselines, Class C the Moderate and Class D the High, though FedRAMP says a class is not an impact level. A FedRAMP Recognized assessor was a 3PAO. Ongoing Certification was continuous monitoring.

sits.line: Layer 5. It verifies. Its Rev5 baselines are selections from the Layer 4 catalog, SP 800-53.

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. The rules launched on 24 June 2026 and took effect on 4 July 2026; the release tagged 2026.11.02.01 was published on 5 November 2026. They name two certification types, 20x and Rev5, two paths, Program and Agency, and Classes A to D. The Choose a Type page says Rev5 ‘will be retired in the future’. The What’s Changing page says continuous monitoring is now Ongoing Certification and that plans of action and milestones ‘have been eliminated entirely’. The Classes page says agencies should not treat classes as one-for-one replacements for the Low, Moderate and High impact levels. The 20x page said on that day that 20x was in Phase 3, with Class D Certifications to be developed in Phase 4.

sources.title: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: the machine-readable rules file

verification.note: Fetched on 14 November 2026. Every ruleset, theme, Key Security Indicator, statement and related control here is that file’s: 17 rulesets and 46 Key Security Indicators in 10 themes. Rule FRC-CSF-BSL lists 155 controls for Rev5 Class B, 322 for Class C and 409 for Class D. Each is one fewer than the legacy workbook’s Low, Moderate and High baselines of 156, 323 and 410, which FedRAMP still publishes marked as legacy: CA-5 is no longer listed. The file writes identifiers as AC-02 (01); they are shown as SP 800-53 prints them, AC-2(1).

sources.title: Important Deadlines, FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026. The page’s Critical Overall Dates: from 1 January 2027 new Rev5 applications and active 20x certifications must follow the Consolidated Rules for 2026; on 11 June 2027 ‘No new applications for FedRAMP Rev5 Certification will be accepted’; on 1 February 2028 all grace periods expire. It also says the rules’ practices expire no later than 31 December 2028.

sources.title: NTC-0004 Initial Outcome from RFC-0020 FedRAMP Authorization Designations

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026: ‘The single official label for all FedRAMP authorizations will be FedRAMP Certification or FedRAMP Certified.’ Class B takes in the former LI-SaaS and Low baselines, Class C the Moderate and Class D the High.

depth.why: The 17 rulesets are listed by name and purpose; their rules are at the source.

nodes.title: Addressing FedRAMP Communication
nodes.text: The Addressing FedRAMP Communication rules (formerly FedRAMP Security Inbox) ensure FedRAMP can reliably contact the security and compliance staff responsible for every FedRAMP-authorized cloud service offering. These rules also set expectations for urgent communications, response time testing, and routing important messages separately from general support or customer service channels.

nodes.title: Agency Use of FedRAMP Certified Cloud Services
nodes.text: The Agency Use rules summarize the many demands made on agencies by the FedRAMP Authorization Act and OMB Memorandum M-24-15 in a simple, clear, easy-to-follow set of FedRAMP-style rules. These rules align agency policies, authorization letters, machine-readable tools, secure configuration review, continuous monitoring, and communication with FedRAMP so certifications can be reused consistently across government.

nodes.title: Collaborative Continuous Monitoring
nodes.text: The Collaborative Continuous Monitoring rules help agencies use shared, current authorization information from providers as part of each agency’s own Information Security Continuous Monitoring strategy. These rules reduce unnecessary manual burden by encouraging automated monitoring and review while allowing each agency to make its own risk-based decisions about ongoing authorization.

nodes.title: Certification Data Sharing
nodes.text: The Certification Data Sharing rules allow providers to store and share FedRAMP Certification Data through the platform they choose as long as it follows FedRAMP rules for access, accuracy, and transparency. This helps customers and the public review consistent, current security and compliance information while recognizing that the information usually remains the provider’s intellectual property and is not federal information.

nodes.title: Cryptographic Module Use
nodes.text: The Cryptographic Module Use rules clarify how providers should select and use cryptographic modules. These rules allow risk-based decisions for some services while still encouraging validated cryptographic modules whenever they are technically feasible and reasonable.

nodes.title: Certification Package Overview
nodes.text: The Certification Package Overview rules outline the expectations for a simple overview of the cloud service offering that must be included within a FedRAMP Certification Package. This overview replaces the historically required base System Security Plan for FedRAMP Rev5 and is intended to provide a clear, concise, and consistent summary of the offering and the information included in the package to help customers understand the offering at a high level.

nodes.title: FedRAMP Certification
nodes.text: This ruleset explains how cloud service offerings obtain and maintain FedRAMP Certification across certification classes and paths.

nodes.title: Incident Evaluation and Communication
nodes.text: The Incident Evaluation and Communication rules explain how providers must communicate incident information to FedRAMP and government customers when they are affected by an incident or likely to be affected by an incident.

nodes.title: Independent Verification and Validation
nodes.text: This ruleset explains the expectations for independent verification and validation assessments.

nodes.title: Minimum Assessment Scope
nodes.text: The Minimum Assessment Scope rules help providers define assessment boundaries narrowly enough to avoid unnecessary review of components that do not affect the offering’s security. These rules still ensure the assessment includes the resources and connections needed to understand the offering’s confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

nodes.title: Marketplace Listing
nodes.text: The Marketplace Listing rules define how FedRAMP decides which cloud service offerings, assessors, and advisors may be listed in the FedRAMP Marketplace. These rules help agencies and other customers rely on the Marketplace as a consistent source of eligible services and supporting organizations, while requiring listed organizations to supply accurate, accessible, and machine-readable information.

nodes.title: FedRAMP Recognition of Independent Assessment Services
nodes.text: The FedRAMP Recognition of independent assessment services rules explain the requirements for assessors to obtain and maintain FedRAMP Recognition in order to support the FedRAMP Certification process.

nodes.title: Secure Configuration Guide
nodes.text: The Secure Configuration Guide rules help agencies and other customers understand how to configure a cloud service offering securely. These rules require providers to clearly explain the security impact of common settings so customers can make informed configuration choices.

nodes.title: Significant Change Notification
nodes.text: The Significant Change Notification rules supply a simple framework allowing providers to make significant changes to their own products while keeping agency customers in the loop. These rules organize significant changes into clear categories so agencies can understand the expected risk and make authorization decisions accordingly.

nodes.title: Security Decision Record
nodes.text: The Security Decision Record replaced a traditional System Security Plan with a persistently maintained, verified, and validated record of the security decisions made by the cloud service provider over the lifecycle of their cloud service offering.

nodes.title: Vulnerability Detection and Response
nodes.text: The Vulnerability Detection and Response rules require providers to continuously identify, analyze, prioritize, mitigate, and remediate vulnerabilities and related exposures through automated systems. These rules give providers flexibility in implementation while ensuring agencies receive the information needed to support ongoing authorization decisions.

nodes.title: Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting
nodes.text: The Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules require cloud service providers to determine when vulnerabilities are likely to impact federal customers and report the status of such vulnerabilities to all necessary parties.

nodes.title: Reviewing All Training
nodes.text: The effectiveness of relevant cybersecurity education and training is persistently reviewed, including at least general training for all employees, role-specific training for employees in high risk roles, training for development and engineering staff on secure software delivery, and training for staff involved with incident response or disaster recovery.

nodes.title: Logging Changes
nodes.text: Modifications to the cloud service offering are logged and monitored.

nodes.title: Redeploying vs Modifying
nodes.text: Changes to machine-based information resources are executed through the redeployment of version controlled resources rather than direct modification wherever reasonable.

nodes.title: Reviewing Change Procedures
nodes.text: The effectiveness of documented change management procedures is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Validating Throughout Deployment
nodes.text: Persistent testing and validation of changes throughout deployment is automated.

nodes.title: Defining Functionality and Privileges
nodes.text: The functionality and privileges for infrastructure and services are strictly defined.

nodes.title: Enforcing Intended State
nodes.text: Automated services are used to persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources and automatically enforce their intended operational state.

nodes.title: Implementing Best Practices
nodes.text: The use and configuration of third-party machine-based information resources is persistently compared against the original provider’s best practices and guidance.

nodes.title: Minimizing Attack Surface
nodes.text: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they have a minimal attack surface and that lateral movement is minimized if compromised.

nodes.title: Optimizing for Availability
nodes.text: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately optimized for high availability and rapid recovery.

nodes.title: Restricting Network Traffic
nodes.text: Machine-based information resources are persistently reviewed to ensure they are appropriately configured to limit inbound and outbound network traffic.

nodes.title: Reviewing Protections
nodes.text: The effectiveness of protection against denial of service attacks and other unwanted activity for machine-based information resources is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Using Logical Networking
nodes.text: Logical networking and related capabilities are used and persistently reviewed to enforce traffic flow controls.

nodes.title: Automating Account Management
nodes.text: The lifecycle and privileges of all accounts, roles, and groups are securely managed using automation.

nodes.title: Adopting Passwordless Methods
nodes.text: Secure passwordless methods are used for user authentication and authorization when feasible, otherwise strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA is used.

nodes.title: Ensuring Least Privilege
nodes.text: Identity and access management measures are used and persistently reviewed to ensure each user or device can only access the resources they need.

nodes.title: Authorizing Just-in-Time
nodes.text: A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time security authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for all user and non-user accounts and services.

nodes.title: Securing Non-User Authentication
nodes.text: Appropriately secure authentication methods are used and persistently reviewed for non-user accounts and services.

nodes.title: Responding to Suspicious Activity
nodes.text: Accounts with privileged access are disabled or otherwise secured in response to suspicious activity.

nodes.title: Generating After Action Reports
nodes.text: Incident after action reports are generated and lessons learned are persistently incorporated.

nodes.title: Reviewing Incident Response Procedures
nodes.text: The effectiveness of documented incident response procedures is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Reviewing Past Incidents
nodes.text: Past incidents are persistently reviewed for patterns or vulnerabilities that were not previously apparent or identified.

nodes.title: Authorizing Log Access
nodes.text: A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time access authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for access to log data based on organizationally defined data sensitivity.

nodes.title: Evaluating Configurations
nodes.text: The configuration of machine-based information resources, especially infrastructure as code, is persistently evaluated and tested.

nodes.title: Logging Event Types
nodes.text: A list of information resources and event types that will be logged, monitored, and audited is maintained and persistently reviewed to ensure these activities occur.

nodes.title: Operating SIEM Capability
nodes.text: A Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or similar system(s) is used and persistently reviewed for centralized, tamper-resistant logging of events, activities, and changes.

nodes.title: Reviewing Logs
nodes.text: Logs are persistently reviewed and audited.

nodes.title: Generating Inventories
nodes.text: Authoritative sources are used to automatically generate real-time inventories of all information resources when needed.

nodes.title: Reviewing Executive Support
nodes.text: Executive support for achieving the provider’s security goals is persistently reviewed and demonstrated.

nodes.title: Reviewing Investments in Security
nodes.text: The effectiveness of the provider’s investments in achieving security goals is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Reviewing Security in the SDLC
nodes.text: The effectiveness of building security and privacy considerations into the Software Development Lifecycle and aligning with CISA Secure By Design principles is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Reviewing Vulnerability Disclosures
nodes.text: The effectiveness of the provider’s vulnerability disclosure program is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Aligning Backups with Objectives
nodes.text: The alignment of machine-based information resource backups with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Aligning Recovery Plan
nodes.text: The alignment of recovery plans with defined recovery objectives is persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Reviewing Recovery Objectives
nodes.text: The desired Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) are defined and persistently reviewed for alignment with the provider’s business needs and capabilities.

nodes.title: Testing Recovery Capabilities
nodes.text: The capability to recover from incidents and contingencies aligned with defined recovery objectives is persistently tested.

nodes.title: Mitigating Supply Chain Risk
nodes.text: Potential supply chain risks are persistently identified, reviewed, and mitigated.

nodes.title: Monitoring Supply Chain Risk
nodes.text: Third party software information resources are automatically monitored for upstream vulnerabilities using mechanisms that may include contractual notification requirements or active monitoring services.

nodes.title: Automating Configuration Management
nodes.text: The configuration of machine-based information resources is managed using automation and persistently reviewed for drift.

nodes.title: Automating Secret Management
nodes.text: Management, protection, and regular rotation of digital keys, certificates, and other secrets is automated and persistently reviewed.

nodes.title: Evaluating and Improving Security
nodes.text: Information resources are persistently evaluated for opportunities to improve security and those improvements are persistently made.

nodes.title: Preventing Residual Risk
nodes.text: Plans, procedures, and the state of information resources are persistently reviewed after making changes to limit and remove unwanted residual elements that would likely negatively affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data.

nodes.title: Removing Unwanted Data
nodes.text: Unwanted federal customer data is removed promptly when requested by an agency in alignment with customer agreements, including from backups if appropriate; this typically applies when a customer spills information or when a customer seeks to remove information from a service due to a change in usage.

nodes.title: Securing Information
nodes.text: Information is encrypted or otherwise secured from unwanted access or modification.

nodes.title: Validating Communications
nodes.text: The authenticity and integrity of communications between machine-based information resources is persistently validated using automation.

nodes.title: Validating Resource Integrity
nodes.text: Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity of machine-based information resources.

sets.name: Rev5 Class B
sets.line: One fewer than the 156 of the legacy Low and LI-SaaS baselines: the 2026 rules no longer list CA-5.

sets.name: Rev5 Class C
sets.line: One fewer than the 323 of the legacy Moderate baseline: the 2026 rules no longer list CA-5.

sets.name: Rev5 Class D
sets.line: One fewer than the 410 of the legacy High baseline: the 2026 rules no longer list CA-5.
